Inbound from product lead at SMB helpdesk vendor; found Redwood via blog on streaming structured output. Early discovery call 2026-02-14. Key asks: easy self-serve hosted API, predictable per-token pricing, tool-calling for ticket actioning (e.g., triage -> apply tags / escalate), structured JSON output for downstream ticketing pipeline, and short summaries for agents and customers.

Highlights from call / quotes:
- 'We need summaries that fit inside our ticket subject + 2-line agent digest.'
- 'Cost is real — we need to remain profitable on free tier customers.'
- Wants routing/fallback that degrades to cheaper model variant when high load.

Technical constraints: mostly public cloud (AWS us-east), lightweight infra, team uses Node + Python. Latency targets: median reply <200ms for 8-32 token responses; p95 <400ms acceptable during peak. Throughput targets: ~30-60 reqs/sec per service during peak, burst to 150 for flash onboarding. Prefers open models / quantized variants but wants Redwood benchmarks.

Security & compliance notes: SSO (SAML) for admin console, audit logs for every API key, KMS integration for encryption at rest. Data retention policy: 30 days by default; may require 90 days for enterprise later. No strict residency right now but prefers US-only storage.

Commercial: SMB price sensitivity; initial POC budget ~ $5k-$10k ARR; potential to grow to $15k ARR if cost-per-ticket looks healthy. Wants simple per-1k-token pricing and burst protection.

CRM shorthand: follow-up: pricing + signup link (Jordan). Tech walkthrough w/ Maya (SE) week of 2026-03-02. Monitor signup conversion after sending sandbox key.
